newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-SPANISH ARMADA SAILS TOWARDS DAVIS CUP SEMIFINALS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SPANISH ARMADA SAILS TOWARDS DAVIS CUP SEMIFINALS.

text.p: Spain's new brigade of hardcourt conquistadors will start hot favourites against Italy as their campaign to lift a first Davis Cup crown gains momentum on Friday.
Spain, with five players in the world's top 20, travel to Pesaro over a weekend in which the United States, Australia and last year's finalists Sweden all seem assured of advancing to the semifinals.
Defying the long-held belief that Spanish players are purely claycourt aficionados, their new Armada have excelled on hardcourts this year.
Carlos Moya, currently ranked eighth in the world, started the ball rolling by reaching the final of the Australian Open in January. He was one of three Spaniards to reach the quarter-finals.
Sergi Bruguera, the 1993 and 1994 French Open champion, proved last week he was now a multi-skilled player when reached the final of the Lipton Championships on a hardcourt.
Ironically, there is no place for the 20th-ranked Bruguera in the team for their indoor quarter-final.
Moya and 12th-ranked Albert Costa will play the singles, while Francis Roig will partner Javier Sanchez in the doubles.
Spain, with more players in the top 20 than any other nation, have been losing finalists on two occasions, in 1965 and 1967, both times against Australia.

Italy have made one change from the team which beat Mexico last month, with Marzio Martelli winning his first Davis Cup cap at the expense of Stefano Pescosolido. Italian number one Renzo Furlan, veteran Omar Camporese and Diego Nargiso all retain their places.
"They have an 80 per cent chance of winning, we have 20 per cent. That seems to me a realistic forecast," Italian newspaper Corriere dello Sport quoted Davis Cup captain Adriano Panatta as saying.
While Spain are sending the cream of their players to Italy, the United States, Netherlands and Czech Republic are missing their top players who have chosen to concentrate on playing the ATP Tour.

With top-ranked players Pete Sampras and Michael Chang sitting out the United States's tie against the Netherlands, a resurgent Jim Courier and severely slumping Andre Agassi will play the singles. Rick Leach and Jonathan Stark will team up for doubles.
Agassi has lost his first match at four tournaments this year, including Lipton, whereas Courier has won in Doha and reached the semifinals in Dubai and at Lipton.

The Netherlands will be missing Wimbledon winner Richard Krajicek, considerably reducing their chances against the 1995 winners. Paul Haarhuis, Jacco Eltingh, Jan Siemerink and Sjeng Schalken make up their team.
"We have a chance if our boys will perform above their abilities," Dutch team captain Stan Franker said ahead of the tie in Newport Beach, California.
Hosts Australia head into their Davis Cup quarter-final against the Czech Republic with their strongest available team in sharp contrast to their troubled opponents.

Czechs Petr Korda, Daniel Vacek, Bohdan Ulihrach and Slava Dosedel have all declined to play. The nation will be represented by Jiri Novak and Martin Damm for the singles, while Pavel Vizner and David Rikl will team up for the doubles.
In contrast, Australia, who bundled out holders France in the previous round in February, will play first-choice pair Mark Philippoussis and Pat Rafter in the singles.
World number one combination Mark Woodforde and Todd Woodbridge will contest the doubles.
Thomas Johansson is on standby for Magnus Larsson, who is suffering a foot injury, for Sweden's clash against South Africa in Vaxjo.
World number seven Thomas Enqvist, Jonas Bjorkman and Nicklas Kulti complete the Swedish team.

Sweden, who lost 3-2 to France in last year's final, start favourites against South Africa, who depend heavily on world number 10 Wayne Ferreira. Grant Stafford, ranked 69, will play the other singles rubber and Ellis Ferreira and David Adams the doubles.
